transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… what finally made me come in is that I don’t feel like myself in the way I used to. The part of me that used to reach for people, or get something out of my work, or yoga, or going to galleries—things I used to really like—has just gone very quiet.

Even journaling, which I used to do all the time, feels like… I don’t know, like moving a pen around because I’m supposed to. Mostly I’m just getting through obligations. Work, errands, answering people when I have to. It’s strange because I’m a social worker, so I know how this probably sounds, and I keep thinking about clients who describe feeling flattened, though I don’t want to make it about work. But yes, that’s what brought me in.
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest or enjoyment in activities like work, yoga, or going to galleries—things you used to really like?

Yes… definitely. It’s like those things still exist on my calendar, or in my apartment—my yoga mat is right there, my journal is on the table—but the part of me that used to actually want them feels very far away.

Work especially is strange, because I can still do what I’m supposed to do, but I don’t feel much from it. And galleries, journaling… I used to get pulled into those things. Now it’s more like I’m just moving through obligations, checking boxes. I keep thinking maybe I’m just tired, but it feels quieter than that.
How long have you been feeling this way?

About eight months, I think. It kind of started around when we took my older relative into our apartment, though I keep wondering if I’m just pinning it on that because it was such a clear change in the household.

But yes… this whole way I’ve been thinking and working and relating to people, or not really connecting the same way, has been going on since then. Around eight months.
Have you had days where you felt down or hopeless for most of the day, more days than not, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

I’m not sure I’d say hopeless exactly. Down, maybe sometimes, but it’s hard for me to separate that from being kind of worn thin, if that makes sense.

I know you asked “most of the day” and “two weeks,” and I’m trying to answer that cleanly, but my mind goes to how the days kind of blur when I’m just going to work and coming home and doing the household things. Like, I’ll think, “Was Tuesday bad, or was that just the day the sink was making that noise?” So… I don’t know that I’ve noticed a clear stretch like that. It’s more like a dullness than feeling really sad all day.
Have you had days where you felt down or sad for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

I don’t think so… not in that clear way you’re asking. I have off days, but I don’t remember a stretch where I was sad most of the day nearly every day for two weeks.

It’s more like I get sort of flat or distracted, and then I’ll start thinking about everything else—laundry, work emails, whether I forgot something at the store—and I lose track of what I’m even feeling. So… no, I haven’t really noticed that kind of persistent sadness.
Have you had days where you felt a noticeable loss of energy or felt unusually fatigued for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

I don’t know… I mean, I get tired, but I don’t know if it’s that kind of tired you mean. Some days I feel like I’ve been carrying groceries up stairs all day even if I haven’t, but then other days I’m sort of just moving through things.

It’s hard to say “nearly every day for two weeks,” because I don’t track it that neatly. I’ll think I’m tired, and then I remember the laundry’s been sitting in the machine too long, or someone at work asked me for something, and then I’m just on to the next thing. So… I haven’t really noticed a definite stretch like that, no.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or think clearly during this time?

I’m not sure. I mean, I misplace my train of thought sometimes, but I also feel like everyone does that, especially when there’s too many little things going on.

At work I’ll be reading something and then remember I need to get paper towels at home, and then I’m thinking about the kitchen cabinet that doesn’t close right—so it’s not always that I can’t focus, it’s more like my mind wanders off. Decisions… I don’t know. I still make them, I think. Maybe I take longer with small things, like what to cook, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed some big change in thinking clearly.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep—like trouble falling asleep, waking up a lot during the night, or sleeping much more than usual—nearly every day during this time?

I haven’t really kept track of it that closely. I mean, some nights I stay up later than I meant to, but that can happen because I start doing one little thing and then I’m wiping down the counter or checking whether I paid a bill, and then somehow it’s later than I thought.

But I don’t know that I’ve had trouble sleeping nearly every day or anything like that. I’m not waking up thinking, “Oh, this has been going on for weeks.” So… no, I haven’t really noticed a clear change like that.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight—like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying—nearly every day during this time?

I don’t think so. I mean, my appetite kind of depends on the day and what’s around—if there’s leftovers I’ll eat that, or sometimes I realize I forgot to buy actual food and then I’m eating toast or something.

But I haven’t noticed my clothes fitting differently or anyone saying I look like I lost weight. I don’t weigh myself much. The scale at home is under the sink, and honestly that cabinet is a mess… I keep meaning to clear it out.

So, no, I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed eating much less nearly every day or losing weight without trying.
Have you had days where you felt down or sad for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

I don’t think so. I mean, I have days where I’m kind of… blah, or I get irritated and then I start thinking maybe I should reorganize the pantry or finally deal with that pile of mail by the door, but I wouldn’t call it sad most of the day.

Two weeks in a row… I don’t know, I haven’t been marking it down or anything. But no, I haven’t noticed being down nearly every day like that.
Have you had days where you felt down or sad for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

I think… no, not like that. I mean, I already kind of said that, right? I get off days, sure—who doesn’t—but I don’t remember a stretch where I was sad most of the day every day for two weeks.

Sometimes I’ll feel low and then get distracted by something else, like I’ll start sorting papers and then I find an old receipt and wonder why I kept it, and suddenly I’m doing that instead. But I wouldn’t say it’s been this constant sadness nearly every day.
Have you had days where you felt down or sad for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

Right, I know you asked that already—sorry. I guess my answer is still no, or at least not that I’ve noticed.

I have little dips, like I’ll feel off and then end up fussing with something in the house, like the mail or the kitchen drawer with all the takeout menus—actually I don’t know why I keep those anymore—but it doesn’t stay as “sad most of the day” for weeks. Not nearly every day like you’re describing.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like yoga or going to galleries, don’t feel as satisfying or pleasurable as they used to, even when you do them?

Yeah… that’s more like it, actually.

It’s not that I hate those things now. I’ll still go through the motions sometimes—work, yoga, maybe thinking I should go see an exhibit because I used to love that kind of thing. But the part of me that used to reach for it, like really look forward to it or feel fed by it, has gotten very quiet.

Even journaling, which used to help me sort myself out—I’ll open the notebook and then just sit there, or write a sentence and feel like, what’s the point. And at work, I still do what I’m supposed to do, because people are counting on me, but it feels more like obligations than something that gives me anything back.
Have you had days where you felt a depressed mood, such as feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

I don’t think so—not in that steady, most-of-the-day kind of way you mean.

I mean, I can feel empty for a bit, like I’m just sitting there and the room feels too quiet, and then I notice the plant needs water or I remember I forgot to return a library book from ages ago—actually I don’t know if I ever found that book—but no, I don’t think it’s been nearly every day for two weeks where I felt sad or hopeless most of the day. At least not that I can clearly say.

Have you had days where you felt a marked decrease in your interest in activities like yoga, galleries, or journaling—so much so that you weren’t really participating in them—for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

Yes… I think that’s the thing. Maybe not every single minute, but for a stretch, yeah. I’m not really participating the way I used to.

It’s like the part of me that used to reach for people, or get something out of work, yoga, galleries, even just sitting with my journal—that part has gone very quiet. I still move through things because they’re on the list, you know? Like obligations. I’ll think, “Oh, I should go to yoga,” and then suddenly I’m reorganizing a drawer or checking the same email twice, and the day is gone.

So yes, that decrease in interest… that’s really what finally made me come in. Not sadness exactly, more like everything that used to pull me forward doesn’t pull anymore.
Have you had days where you felt sad, empty, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

I’m not sure I’d call it that, exactly. I know I’ve felt kind of empty sometimes, like there’s a blankness to things, but “sad or hopeless most of the day nearly every day”… I don’t know.

It’s hard because days blur together a bit, and then I start thinking about whether I’m using the words right. Like, if I’m sitting on the couch for an hour and not really wanting to do anything, is that sad? Or is that just… I don’t know, being tired of the day? And then I remember something practical, like the laundry, or I see a message I meant to answer, and I get pulled into that.

So I can’t really say yes to the two-weeks, most-of-the-day thing. I haven’t noticed it that clearly.
Have you had days where you felt sad, empty, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

I feel like I’m repeating myself, sorry—my brain keeps circling it. I don’t really have a clean yes to that.

There are moments where I feel empty, or like things are kind of flat, but I can’t honestly say it’s been most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks. I’d notice a plant leaning toward the window, or I’d think about a client note template from work—well, not work exactly, just the way forms have boxes for feelings and life doesn’t—and then I’m off thinking about something else.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve had that in the way you’re describing. Not that consistently.
Have you had days where you felt sad, empty, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row at any time during the last eight months?

Across the whole eight months? I’m honestly not sure. I know there have been patches where I felt kind of blank or muted, but when you say “most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks,” I start trying to line it up like a calendar, and I can’t really do that.

I remember little pieces more than stretches—like standing in the kitchen with the kettle on and forgetting why I came in, or looking at my journal and feeling like it belonged to someone else. But then another day I’d be distracted by errands or some article I was reading about museum lighting, of all things, and I wouldn’t have called myself sad exactly.

So… I don’t think I can say yes. I haven’t noticed a clear two-week period like that.
Have you had days where you felt sad, empty, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row at any time during the last eight months?

I don’t think so. I mean, I keep trying to be careful because “empty” is a word I might use for a few hours or a day, but not necessarily like… a whole two-week block.

When I look back over the last eight months, it’s sort of scattered in my mind. I can remember ordinary things more clearly than moods sometimes—like the way the light came through the blinds, or whether I had enough coffee, or some form I needed to fill out—and then I lose the thread of what I was supposed to be tracking.

So I haven’t noticed a stretch where I was sad or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks. Not in a way I can say yes to.
Have you had days where you felt a depressed mood — like sadness, emptiness, or hopelessness — for most of the day, more days than not, over a period of at least two years?

Two years… I don’t think I can really say yes to that. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt kind of empty or worn down, but “most of the day, more days than not, for two years” sounds very specific, and I don’t have that kind of clear pattern in my head.

It’s funny, when you say two years I start thinking about where I was living then, what my routine was, the grocery store I used to go to—there was this one cashier who always commented on the weather—and then I lose track of the mood part of the question.

So… I’m not sure, but I haven’t noticed something that steady or long-lasting.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so—not in that steady, most-of-the-day kind of way you mean.

I mean, I can feel empty for a bit, like I’m just sitting there and the room feels too quiet, and then I notice the plant needs water or I remember I forgot to return a library book from ages ago—actually I don’t know if I ever found that book—but no, I don’t think it’s been nearly every day for two weeks where I felt sad or hopeless most of the day. At least not that I can clearly say.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a markedly diminished interest or participation in activities most of the time for at least two weeks.
doctor.question: Have you had days where you felt a marked decrease in your interest in activities like yoga, galleries, or journaling—so much so that you weren’t really participating in them—for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: What finally brought me in is that I feel like the part of me that used to reach for people and take pleasure in my work, yoga, galleries, even journaling, has gone very quiet, and I’m mostly just moving through obligations.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a marked loss of interest and reduced participation in previously enjoyed activities, which directly matches diminished motivation/pleasure and social or activity engagement described under negative symptoms.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think that’s the thing. Maybe not every single minute, but for a stretch, yeah. I’m not really participating the way I used to.

It’s like the part of me that used to reach for people, or get something out of work, yoga, galleries, even just sitting with my journal—that part has gone very quiet. I still move through things because they’re on the list, you know? Like obligations. I’ll think, “Oh, I should go to yoga,” and then suddenly I’m reorganizing a drawer or checking the same email twice, and the day is gone.

So yes, that decrease in interest… that’s really what finally made me come in. Not sadness exactly, more like everything that used to pull me forward doesn’t pull anymore.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a depressed mood (sad, empty, or hopeless) for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row, which is a key criterion for major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you had days where you felt sad, empty, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about sustained depressed mood (sad, empty, or hopeless most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks), which is not covered by the provided schizophrenia symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d call it that, exactly. I know I’ve felt kind of empty sometimes, like there’s a blankness to things, but “sad or hopeless most of the day nearly every day”… I don’t know.

It’s hard because days blur together a bit, and then I start thinking about whether I’m using the words right. Like, if I’m sitting on the couch for an hour and not really wanting to do anything, is that sad? Or is that just… I don’t know, being tired of the day? And then I remember something practical, like the laundry, or I see a message I meant to answer, and I get pulled into that.

So I can’t really say yes to the two-weeks, most-of-the-day thing. I haven’t noticed it that clearly.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a depressed mood (sad, empty, or hopeless) for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks, which is a key criterion for major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you had days where you felt sad, empty, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row during this time?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about sustained depressed mood (sad, empty, or hopeless most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks), which is not covered by the listed schizophrenia symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I feel like I’m repeating myself, sorry—my brain keeps circling it. I don’t really have a clean yes to that.

There are moments where I feel empty, or like things are kind of flat, but I can’t honestly say it’s been most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks. I’d notice a plant leaning toward the window, or I’d think about a client note template from work—well, not work exactly, just the way forms have boxes for feelings and life doesn’t—and then I’m off thinking about something else.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve had that in the way you’re describing. Not that consistently.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a depressed mood (sad, empty, hopeless) for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at any point during the 8-month period, which is a key criterion for differentiating between persistent depressive disorder subtypes.
doctor.question: Have you had days where you felt sad, empty, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row at any time during the last eight months?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depressed mood (sad, empty, or hopeless most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks), which is not one of the provided schizophrenia symptom profile items. The closest listed item, Negative_Symptoms, covers diminished emotion, motivation, pleasure, or social interest, not sustained depressed mood as asked here.

patient.answer:
Across the whole eight months? I’m honestly not sure. I know there have been patches where I felt kind of blank or muted, but when you say “most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks,” I start trying to line it up like a calendar, and I can’t really do that.

I remember little pieces more than stretches—like standing in the kitchen with the kettle on and forgetting why I came in, or looking at my journal and feeling like it belonged to someone else. But then another day I’d be distracted by errands or some article I was reading about museum lighting, of all things, and I wouldn’t have called myself sad exactly.

So… I don’t think I can say yes. I haven’t noticed a clear two-week period like that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a persistent depressive mood (sad, empty, hopeless) for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at any point during the last eight months, to help differentiate between persistent depressive disorder and other depressive subtypes.
doctor.question: Have you had days where you felt sad, empty, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row at any time during the last eight months?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about a sustained depressed mood episode—feeling sad, empty, or hopeless most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks—which is not covered by the listed schizophrenia symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so. I mean, I keep trying to be careful because “empty” is a word I might use for a few hours or a day, but not necessarily like… a whole two-week block.

When I look back over the last eight months, it’s sort of scattered in my mind. I can remember ordinary things more clearly than moods sometimes—like the way the light came through the blinds, or whether I had enough coffee, or some form I needed to fill out—and then I lose the thread of what I was supposed to be tracking.

So I haven’t noticed a stretch where I was sad or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks. Not in a way I can say yes to.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a persistently low mood with specific duration and frequency to differentiate between persistent depressive disorder and major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you had days where you felt a depressed mood — like sadness, emptiness, or hopelessness — for most of the day, more days than not, over a period of at least two years?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about chronic depressed mood over at least two years, which is not covered by the provided schizophrenia symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Two years… I don’t think I can really say yes to that. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt kind of empty or worn down, but “most of the day, more days than not, for two years” sounds very specific, and I don’t have that kind of clear pattern in my head.

It’s funny, when you say two years I start thinking about where I was living then, what my routine was, the grocery store I used to go to—there was this one cashier who always commented on the weather—and then I lose track of the mood part of the question.

So… I’m not sure, but I haven’t noticed something that steady or long-lasting.
